description: My project, *Little Mars*, is a browser-based game where players manage a Martian outpost, grow food, balance limited resources, and protect their crew from space weather. It uses real NASA space-weather observations within simplified gameplay, giving players opportunities to learn through choices and consequences.
summary:
Little Mars: Storm Watch is an interactive 3D Mars colony-survival game that challenges players to lead a Martian outpost through a five-Sol mission. Players explore the Martian environment, operate rovers, develop their colony, conduct research, and manage essential resources such as oxygen, food, and power while responding to environmental hazards.

A key feature of our project is its integration of NASA's CCMC DONKI space-weather data, connecting gameplay with real-world solar activity and radiation risks that could affect future Mars missions. Through interactive science activities, research, mission alerts, and educational guidance, players gain a better understanding of the challenges of human exploration beyond Earth.

Our goal is to transform complex space-science concepts into an engaging and accessible learning experience, encouraging curiosity about planetary science, engineering, space weather, and the future of human settlement on Mars.

Our team worked collaboratively under a tight deadline, dividing responsibilities according to individual strengths and areas of expertise. By combining our skills in programming, visual design, image creation, and research, we maximized our collective potential and brought together multiple features into a functional experience.

A Sol (Martian day) is the length of one complete day on Mars, measured from one sunrise to the next.
- 1 Earth day: 24 hours
- 1 Martian Sol: approximately 24 hours, 39 minutes, 35 seconds.
details:
Project Details

Gameplay and Core Mechanics

Little Mars: Storm Watch is an interactive 3D Mars colony-survival game built around a five-Sol mission. Players take on the role of mission commanders and make decisions that determine the survival and development of their Martian outpost. They can explore the Martian environment, operate rovers, construct colony facilities, develop agriculture, conduct scientific research, and manage essential resources such as oxygen, food, and power. Players must also respond to environmental hazards and make strategic decisions to keep their colony operational.

NASA Data Integration and Scientific Learning

A key feature of our project is its integration of NASA's CCMC DONKI space-weather data. The game introduces players to real space-weather events and demonstrates how solar activity can create radiation risks for astronauts and affect missions beyond Earth. Its Live and Archive modes connect gameplay with real-world space-weather information. Through research activities, science checks, mission alerts, and educational guidance, players learn about the scientific challenges of establishing a sustainable human presence on Mars.

Technology and Development

We developed the project using JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Three.js to create an interactive 3D experience. We incorporated NASA space-weather data and developed systems for resource management, exploration, colony development, mission progression, and educational interaction.

Visual Design and Asset Creation

We focused on creating an immersive visual experience through visual design and image creation. Our team developed and incorporated visual assets to bring the Martian environment, colony, interfaces, and gameplay elements to life. We aimed for a cohesive space-themed design that would make the experience visually engaging while keeping navigation and information accessible.

Creativity, Accessibility, and Impact

The project combines simulation, exploration, and learning into one experience. Features such as astronaut customization, different mission settings, achievements, a science laboratory, and the Pip guide make the experience more engaging. We also included parent and teacher guides to support learning beyond the game itself. Our goal is to encourage curiosity about planetary science, space weather, engineering, and the challenges of future human exploration.

Team Collaboration

Working under a tight deadline, we divided responsibilities among team members according to individual strengths. Through collaboration, communication, and shared problem-solving, we maximized our collective potential and brought together multiple features into a functional project within a limited timeframe.
